practice.mast: Across {count_word} works, sources, constraints, failures, and reader actions remain attached to the forms they help produce.
intro: The work often begins when a material no longer fits its first container. A source grows too charged for a footnote; a short poem asks for darkness around it; a system notice keeps speaking after its promise of recovery has thinned; a dramatic scene begins to behave like a procedure.
No fixed sequence joins research, writing, interface, and code. Their relation is composed anew for each work.

modules.title: Research can return
modules.home_text: A source can remain reachable after it enters a literary arrangement.
modules.text: Speculative research poetry keeps the origin and limits of a source visible instead of letting a poem quietly absorb it. A source-bearing scene can acquire its own address inside the field, a location a reader can return to independently of the line it helped produce. The source stays available rather than exhausted by what a poem does with it — a working version of what object-oriented ontology calls withdrawal, built here into the interface rather than argued as philosophy.
modules.alt: The Black Bird Reader beside its graph
modules.caption: A source-bearing object remains inside the field.

modules.title: Writing through constraints
modules.home_text: Rules of recurrence give authorship a temporal and procedural form.
modules.text: Generative writing places authorship inside the conditions of recurrence rather than outside them: a rule, a word bank, a timing pattern becomes where a decision actually gets made. One construction can carry real weight under its own pressure, tested against material it did not choose. Elsewhere in the practice, the construction itself is opened to revision — a rule set moves from infrastructure into something an author can work directly, so the constraint is rewritten as much as it is run. What gets kept, weighted, and allowed to recur is the writing.
modules.alt: Grave-Machine generated lines beside a runtime trace
modules.caption: The poem accumulates beside the record of its formation.

modules.title: The interface carries consequence
modules.home_text: Visibility, duration, movement, and return participate in the writing.
modules.text: Interface choices are not neutral delivery for these works; they participate in what gets written. Nearness can govern visibility, so that a passage is not simply revealed but temporarily held, then let recede — reading becomes a duration rather than an access event. Elsewhere, a familiar system convention keeps speaking after its ordinary promise has thinned, letting the interface itself carry a piece's real subject. The commitment underneath is closer to a scenographer's use of light and staged visibility than to a screen designer's: what a reader can reach, and when, is authored with the same attention as what they read.
modules.alt: UNHAPPY Scenario reconnecting notice beside accumulated lines
modules.caption: A familiar system notice acquires another duration.

home_teaser.title: The form is discovered through the material
home_teaser.text: Research, writing, interface, and code meet differently in each work. Their relation is composed anew rather than applied as a house style.

about.mast: Mohammad Zare (Mozare) is an Iranian poet and researcher. Mozare is the artistic name used for the works; Mohammad Zare remains the name used for academic records, citations, rights, and professional identification.
paragraphs: Mohammad Zare is an Iranian poet, researcher, and product/interface practitioner. His work joins dramatic literature to browser-based forms and attends to moments when writing remains visibly attached to its sources, procedures, failures, or reader actions.

He completed a BSc in Industrial Engineering at Sharif University of Technology (2015–2020) and an MA in Dramatic Literature at the University of Art, Tehran (2020–2024). His practical and theoretical work has moved through playwriting, speculative research poetry, critical writing, translation, curatorial work, generative literature, and interface design.

The {count_word} works in this portfolio are where those trajectories currently meet. They are presented under the name Mozare; the formal name, Mohammad Zare, remains attached to citations, rights, the CV, and academic records.

works.title: The Black Bird
works.summary: A black bird appears beside a body, and other scenes gather around that contact. Each source, name, object, and relation receives an address without being closed into one explanation.
works.meta_description: The Black Bird is a hypergraph research poem by Mozare. The reader moves between a field of linked materials and the text held in its Reader.
works.hero_lead: A black bird appears beside a body. The scene does not remain singular. It draws other materials toward it, each carrying its own form and degree of support.

views.title: Three views
views.intro: Three images hold distinct reading conditions without reducing the work to a single representative screen.

items.title: Threshold
items.text: Entry before the field becomes visible.

items.title: Mapping note
items.text: A local poetic surface remains linked to the wider relation field.

items.title: Relation field
items.text: Objects, names, sources, and relation bodies remain simultaneously addressable.

context.title: A field that keeps its differences
paragraphs: The Black Bird gives each material a distinct working body. Research notes carry source-bearing prose. Mapping notes condense charged relations into local textual surfaces. Recurring things receive stable addresses, while names and citations preserve routes of return.

These distinctions let research and poetry remain in contact without asking one to borrow the authority of the other. The field makes contact spatial; the Reader gives one object time; Route records a partial movement through the work.

annex.label: RESEARCH ANNEX
annex.title: Speculative Indices v1.0
paragraphs: The work's first research annex, Speculative Indices for a Research-Field (2026), counts what the field already holds. Two matrices carry the calculation. The first records which of the eighteen Field Objects appear in each of the four source-bearing Research Note Objects; the second records which Field Objects take part in each of the twelve Relation Objects. Three index families follow: Object Incidence, how often an object recurs across the research notes; Relational Thickness, how often two objects share a note or a relation; and Mediational Incidence, how many relations hold an object.

The indices give recurrence and mediation a small surface, so a reader can return to the field knowing where it has already thickened. Their first finding is a difference the graph alone does not show. Black Bird and Corpse each appear in all four research notes, but nine of the twelve relations hold Corpse and eight hold Black Bird: the object that opens the work and the densest relation-body are not the same.

works.title: Winter Road
works.summary: Nine haiku inhabit a dark field that withholds them from a single view. A poem becomes legible through proximity, can be held briefly, then recedes as attention moves elsewhere.
works.responsibility: a poem can remain hidden until approached
works.meta_description: Winter Road is a digital haiga space by Mozare in which nine English haiku are found through movement and held only for a time.
works.hero_lead: Nine English haiku inhabit a dark field. None is presented as the next item in a sequence. The reader searches by moving and finds that another poem can begin to surface elsewhere.

context.title: A haiga space
paragraphs: The nine poems began around two words: winter road. Repeated rewriting moved some words, removed others, and allowed several to return under new grammatical pressure. The result is a family of completed haiku without a single poem serving as the original.
In the browser, the poems coexist without becoming equally available. Darkness gives distance a role, makes discovery local, and lets the field recover after a poem fades.

works.title: UNHAPPY Scenario
works.summary: Software calls the route away from success an unhappy scenario. The phrase makes interruption sound manageable: a branch to be anticipated, named, and recovered from.
works.responsibility: procedural language can retain the memory of blackout
works.meta_description: UNHAPPY Scenario is an internet blackout poem by Mozare, made from the calm procedural language of system failure and repeated interruption.
works.hero_lead: Software calls the route away from success an unhappy scenario. The phrase makes interruption sound manageable: a branch to be anticipated, named, and recovered from.

items.label: 01 / TIME
items.title: Allow one continuous interval
items.note: The work keeps its own durations.

items.label: 02 / WINDOW
items.title: Give it the whole browser
items.note: The black surface is composed as one field.

items.label: 03 / PRIVACY
items.title: Nothing leaves the browser
items.note: No file, message, report, analytics request, cookie, or persistent storage is used.

views.title: Three notices
views.intro: The images keep each view inside the surface that gives it pressure. They document the work without replacing its duration.

items.title: Upload failed
items.text: A pale image remains close to arrival. The notice is calm enough to belong anywhere.

items.title: Reconnecting…
items.text: The ellipsis holds the promise open. Its duration becomes more legible than its assurance.

items.title: Reporting failed
items.text: The language of accountability reaches a sentence that cannot reach its recipient.

context.title: The calm language of interruption
paragraphs: UNHAPPY Scenario stays with that calm language after recovery has ceased to be credible. Drawn from the small notices through which systems explain failure and promise return, the poem carries their familiar English into the memory of repeated internet blackouts in Iran.

What begins as technical inconvenience becomes a vocabulary for isolation, deferred contact, and an accountability that cannot be reached. The notices keep their procedural composure; under blackout, that composure becomes one of the work’s pressures.
context.coda: The title keeps the managerial calm of the phrase and the conditions it cannot contain.

context.title: From dramatic material to generative return
paragraphs: Grave was written as the practical component of Mohammad Zare’s MA in Dramatic Literature. Its scenes place bodies beside paperwork; rooms become processing sites, and burial begins to resemble administration.

Grave-Machine extracts this field of pressure rather than adapting the play as plot. The English and Persian versions share one runtime while retaining distinct materials, grammatical devices, language direction, and typographic proportions.

works.title: TAROKO REMIXER
works.form: A no-code platform for procedural poems
works.summary: Taroko Gorge kept its word lists in plain view, and writers changed them to make poems of their own. TAROKO REMIXER turns those decisions into modules, so a working poem-machine can be designed, run, and exported without writing code.
works.responsibility: a remix can be made without writing code
works.meta_description: TAROKO REMIXER is a browser-native no-code platform by Mohammad Zare (Mozare) for composing, running, and exporting procedural poems in the remix lineage of Nick Montfort's Taroko Gorge (2009).
works.hero_lead: Nick Montfort's Taroko Gorge (2009) kept its word lists in plain view, and writers copied the page, changed the words, and published their own versions. TAROKO REMIXER carries that openness toward no-code creation: banks, routes, stanzas, and rules become modules wired together in the browser.

views.title: Three views
views.intro: Three images hold distinct reading conditions without reducing the work to a single representative screen.

items.title: Materials
items.text: Banks hold Materials with weights and roles. The Taroko Gorge baseline arrives as seven Banks and fifty Materials, each editable in place.
items.alt: TAROKO REMIXER: the Materials chamber with Banks and Materials

items.title: Instruments
items.text: Inputs receive Materials, and weighted Routes turn them into lines through templates such as {above} {trans} {below}.
items.alt: TAROKO REMIXER: the Instruments chamber with Inputs and Routes

items.title: Unmix
items.text: A line taken from the running Surface opens the Flow, Stanza, Instrument, Route, Materials, and Rules that produced it.
items.alt: TAROKO REMIXER: Unmix trace for a generated line

context.title: A platform for remixes
paragraphs: At the Electronic Literature Organization's 2012 panel “Taroko Gorge Remixed,” Sonny Rae Tempest, speaking “from a non-academic place” and without knowing JavaScript, described using Montfort's poem “as a template”: the code was simple enough that friends could see the input and the output and “go and do this themselves.” That simplicity is one reason a remix lineage grew around Taroko Gorge.

TAROKO REMIXER follows that aspect toward no-code creation. The decisions a remixer once made inside the source file (which words, in which Banks, with what weights, through which line patterns, in what order, under which exceptions) become modules that are configured and wired in the browser. A person can design a working poem-machine, run it, and export it as a standalone HTML work without writing a line of code.

Every programming language is an interface over a more basic one, and no-code carries that track further toward access. Montfort and Bogost's platform studies (Racing the Beam, 2009, and the Platform Studies series) give a name to what the app becomes: a platform for an open-ended number of procedural e-poems, each of them a remix. Fifteen works from the Taroko Gorge lineage, Montfort's original among them, can be opened as editable baselines.
context.coda: After Nick Montfort, Taroko Gorge (2009). The bundled baselines remain the work of their authors.

works.title: Hamlet Pop-Upper
works.summary: Hamlet's question enters the recurring procedure of a popup. A stored answer and a deferred question meet a fixed score of deaths moving on its own time.
works.responsibility: an interface carries an answer forward; the next encounter gives it authority again
works.meta_description: Hamlet Pop-Upper is Mohammad Zare's browser-native miniature adaptation, composing Hamlet's question through popup recurrence, stored choice, deferral, and a fixed score of deaths.
works.hero_lead: Father is dead before the first question appears. Hamlet's sentence then returns through an apparatus that remembers selections, schedules deferrals, and meets each death in another state.

items.label: 01 / TIME
items.title: Allow about ninety seconds for one uninterrupted encounter.

items.label: 02 / SOUND
items.title: Sound is optional and begins only after visitor input.

items.label: 03 / MEMORY
items.title: “Remember this answer” stores the selected answer in this browser.

views.title: Three views
views.intro: Three images hold distinct reading conditions without reducing the work to a single representative screen.

items.title: The question
items.text: The popup carries “To be” and “Not to be” as two selectable states.

items.title: The encounter
items.text: A scored death crosses the current state of the asking apparatus and marks its surface.

items.title: The afterimage
items.text: After the final dialog closes, its skull-like afterimage sits behind the accumulated list of deaths.

context.title: Two inherited forms
paragraphs: Hamlet Pop-Upper works with two inherited forms: Hamlet's question and the popup's procedure for interrupting attention, requesting a decision, retaining a selection, and returning. Their contact becomes the material of the adaptation. Literary language enters an interface process; the interface acquires a dramatic role.

The work uses an in-page HTML dialog rather than a separate browser window. The fixed death score and the visitor's variable responses keep separate times inside that dialog. Each death is classified by the state it encounters, and the classification changes the line, position, and density of the trace left on the apparatus. A remembered answer therefore participates in later events as active state, while a deferral composes the interval in which an event may arrive.
context.coda: The selection persists as data. At the next call, the person decides how it speaks for them.

identity.encounter: Answer, remember, or defer; the score keeps its own time
